posts.text:
It’s a rare find but a few times in my career at Sprott I was able to dig up stocks that I could model with reasonable assumptions that I thought where trading at a P/E sub 3 a just 2-3 years out.  With a shot at they they could be at a P/E or 1.

Felix Coal was one of those examples.  New mine was scheduled to come on with existing mine financing the growth.  Coal prices took off more than expected and it ended up that the original shares we bought were 1/2 x 3 years out earnings.  Stock 20x and got bought out by a major.    Huge deposit that started with a 1 to 1 strip ratio.

Wall Street and Bay Street typical only model 2 years out earnings and the market pays little attention to 3 years out.  By doing the work and considering what is possible and likely 3-5 years out is how you find 10x stocks. 

The best ones for me have always been the companies that I think the worst case it’s a double because it still cheap and a double over 10 years is still 7% annualized.  A double over 5 years is near 15% annualized.

I prefer investments that I think I’ll get the double with conservative estimates but there’s still a chance that I could get 10-20x if things go very well.  

With these sorts of investments if things go well and time passes just a year or two into the investment I’ve often gotten a massive rerating. 

The catalysts / achievements I expected are recognized by the market and more investors begin modeling the potential revenue and earnings growth as it comes closer to being real and near term.  

I always have said sure doubles come when possible ten baggers are simply recognized by a broader audience.  Most investors never get a ten bagger and are happy to invest in things that look like 2,3 or 5x returns.  So as a possible 10x is examined by a larger audience it doubles just due to a broader audience.

In my book, I detail my style of investing and hard lessons I learned while trying to optimize my mind, body and financial habits
